meta_notes.scope: doc 27 SS8, frozen BEFORE any number existed: no outcome of exp44 is a quantum-advantage result. One rung, one task family, one dataset, simulation only, 6 verbs, 5 seeds. A favourable result says a 14-parameter model beats 16- and 256-parameter classical models at a swap-sensitivity task -- a statement about model classes on this task, nothing more. The C1 margin from Phase 2 stays narrow (0.7993 vs a 0.7933 permutation 95th percentile) and every quotation of tier-q carries it.
meta_notes.budget_asymmetry: doc 27 SS4 F1+F2, DELIBERATE and in the COMPARATORS' favour: B4/B5 receive 60 full epochs at each of 4 configs with per-seed val-only selection, i.e. up to 8x A2's optimiser steps (72000 at batch 1 vs A2's 9000) and 4x its hyperparameter search (A2 ran at one frozen config). Admissible under doc 24 SS3 because it can only make our own claim harder. This asymmetry MUST be stated in every report of the result (Rule 5), including a favourable one.
meta_notes.narrowing_rule_if_B4_wins: doc 27 SS7, frozen: if tier_q_B4_passed is false, tier_q_passed in results_exp43b_phase2.json STANDS AS COMPUTED (it was registered as A2 vs B1), but its interpretation narrows to 'A2 beats the structure-matched classical arm B1; an unconstrained classical arm of matched parameter count does not lose.' That narrowing travels with the tier-q number into every README, PDF, slide and conversation, and is stated BEFORE the tier-q number, not after it.
